title: First London Underground Railway Opens
description: On January 10, 1863, the world's first underground railway, the Metropolitan Railway, opened in London. The initial 3.75-mile line ran between Paddington and Farringdon, carrying 38,000 passengers on its first day. Steam locomotives pulled wooden carriages through gas-lit tunnels, revolutionizing urban transportation. This pioneering achievement established London as a leader in public transit innovation and set the blueprint for subway systems worldwide. Today, the London Underground (the Tube) serves over 1 billion passengers annually.
